pr_title: test_runner: allow special characters in snapshot keys
pr_body:
Use `JSONStringify` to serialise snapshot keys to allow special characters such as `\r` to be used in test names

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/56836

issue_context.title: Test runner cannot find snapshot with `\r` in title
issue_context.body:
### Version

23.7.0

### Platform

```text
- my PC: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64
- ubuntu-latest on GitHub Actions
- windows-latest on GitHub Actions
```

### Subsystem

Test runner

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

`test.ts`:

```typescript
import {test} from 'node:test';

test('\r', t => {
	t.assert.snapshot({json: 'value'});
});
```

```bash
$ node --test-update-snapshots test.ts
$ node --test test.ts
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

It should be able to select the correct snapshot that it has just written.

### What do you see instead?

```plain
✖ failing tests:

test at test.ts:3:1
 (2.8696ms)
 1' not found in '[...]\node-test-snapshot-cr\test.ts.snapshot.' Missing snapshots can be generated by rerunning the command with the --test-update-snapshots flag.
      at SnapshotFile.getSnapshot (node:internal/test_runner/snapshot:69:19)
      at TestContext.snapshotAssertion (node:internal/test_runner/snapshot:206:41)
      at assert.<computed> [as snapshot] (node:internal/test_runner/test:254:18)
      at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///[...]/node-test-snapshot-cr/test.ts:4:11)
      at Test.runInAsyncScope (node:async_hooks:211:14)
      at Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:980:25)
      at Test.start (node:internal/test_runner/test:878:17)
      at startSubtestAfterBootstrap (node:internal/test_runner/harness:297:17) {
    code: 'ERR_INVALID_STATE',
    snapshot: '\r 1',
    filename: '[...]\\node-test-snapshot-cr\\test.ts.snapshot'
  }
```

### Additional information

- https://github.com/melusc/node-test-snapshot-cr
- https://github.com/melusc/node-test-snapshot-cr/actions/runs/13065943568

review_comments:
I'm not sure about this approach: updating the test snapshot shouldn't be necessary after it's first created.
This way, it seems we're just verifying that a snapshot file is being created, and I imagine this test would still pass even if we removed the fix.

WDYT? @Ceres6

We're actually not asserting anything about the creation process, just that we're able to read from the created file.

If we removed the fix it would fail because the snapshot would be updated with the previous (incorrect) serialization and we wouldn't be able to read it anymore

My bad, I missed the second run!  
I'm still a little bit confused about the need to save the snapshot.  
If our goal is only to verify that we can save and read it, is it still needed?

Except for this, it makes sense to me.

Edit: if it's not needed could https://nodejs.org/api/test.html#snapshotsetresolvesnapshotpathfn help us avoid saving an unnecessary file?
It is not needed, I just didn't know how to avoid saving it! I'll take a look

I think the bug happens while reading the snapshots back. I think for this case, it would be better to test a full round trip (write the file and then read it back) using the public APIs. It would probably be good to check a couple more cases besides just `\r` since in https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/56836#issuecomment-2629256211, it was reported that this happens for a range of inputs (not saying we should test every single input though).
The test was failing before the check, but I will add an e2e test
AFAICS the range in that comment is the block of high surrogate and low surrogate pairs which are reserved for utf-16 and shouldn't appear, but I'm not an expert on this, so not sure
